*ZetSol Energy | A Zetwerk Company | Solar Manufacturing & Supply Chain Platform for North America*

**Position:** Director – Operations 
**Location:** North Carolina/ South Carolina 
**Type:** Full-Time 
**Reports To:** CEO, ZetSol Energy

**Who We Are**

ZetSol Energy is the solar manufacturing and supply chain platform built to give North American solar developers, EPCs, utilities, and independent power producers a reliable, tariff-compliant alternative to fragmented overseas sourcing. The company is establishing a vertically integrated greenfield facility in Tuticorin, Tamil Nadu, producing silicon ingots, monocrystalline wafers, cells, and modules, including high-efficiency TOPCon and HJT technology, and pairs that manufacturing base with a full strategic sourcing, bill-of-materials management, quality audit, compliance, and logistics practice purpose-built for the US market.

ZetSol Energy is backed by Zetwerk, a global manufacturing platform valued at over $2.7 billion that already supplies solar piles, mechanical and structural components, and modules to leading US EPCs and asset owners, and whose 2022 acquisition of Unimacts strengthened its US industrial and solar manufacturing footprint. ZetSol Energy is the next chapter of that build-out: a dedicated US-facing commercial platform launching at a moment when American solar developers are actively searching for supply chain partners who can deliver both scale and certainty.

**The Opportunity**

We are looking for an experienced operations leader to lead and scale ZetSol Energy's US operations, with overall responsibility for manufacturing, factory production, supply chain, logistics and sales operations.

The ideal candidate will have extensive experience in managing large-scale operations, with a strong background in Supply Chain Management (SCM), logistics and manufacturing, preferably within the renewable energy, solar or industrial sectors.

This individual will be responsible for overseeing factory production, managing end-to-end supply chain and logistics operations, and driving sales operations, including demand planning, order management and customer fulfilment in the US market.

The role will also involve building strong relationships with US government authorities, regulatory bodies, logistics partners and other key industry stakeholders, while ensuring operational efficiency, regulatory compliance and cost optimisation.

This is a key leadership position that will play an instrumental role in building and scaling ZetSol Energy's US operations, establishing robust operational processes and driving business growth in North America.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead and oversee end-to-end US operations for ZetSol Energy, covering manufacturing, supply chain, logistics and sales operations.
* Manage factory production operations, including production planning, capacity utilisation, quality, productivity and timely delivery.
* Drive end-to-end supply chain and logistics operations, including global sourcing, procurement, inventory management, import/export, customs clearance and distribution.
* Oversee sales operations, including demand planning, order management, customer fulfilment and coordination with commercial teams.
* Build and manage relationships with US government authorities, regulatory bodies, customs officials, port authorities, logistics partners and other key stakeholders.
* Ensure compliance with US trade regulations, import policies, tariffs and applicable industry standards while driving operational efficiency and cost optimisation.
* Build and scale the US operations team, processes and infrastructure while working closely with the leadership and manufacturing teams in India.

**Qualifications**

* 15–20 years of experience in operations, manufacturing, supply chain management and logistics, preferably within renewable energy, solar, infrastructure or industrial sectors.
* Extensive experience managing large-scale manufacturing operations, including factory production, production planning, quality and operational efficiency.
* Strong experience in end-to-end supply chain, logistics and sales operations, including global sourcing, procurement, import/export, order management and customer fulfilment.
* Strong understanding of US trade regulations, import compliance, tariffs, customs procedures and logistics frameworks.
* Established relationships with government authorities, regulatory bodies, customs officials, port authorities and key industry stakeholders.
* Proven track record of building and managing large operational teams, vendor ecosystems and strategic partnerships, with strong commercial and cost management capabilities.

**Desired Qualifications**

* Experience in the solar, renewable energy or energy manufacturing ecosystem.
* Previous experience leading operations for a global manufacturing or industrial organisation.
* Experience managing manufacturing facilities and cross-border operations between the US and international markets, preferably India.
* Ability to build and scale operational infrastructure in a fast-growing business environment.

**Why ZetSol Energy**

* Opportunity to play a key leadership role in building ZetSol Energy's US operations.
* Work closely with the CEO and leadership team in shaping the company's operational strategy.
* Opportunity to build and scale a large operational and supply chain ecosystem.
* Be part of a growing solar manufacturing and supply chain platform backed by Zetwerk's global manufacturing capabilities.

identity_held_roles.description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

You will lead Huntsville manufacturing for the BE-4 and Northstar engines—powerful engines that support Blue Origin’s launch vehicles and our mission to build a road to space. Reporting to the Vice President of Engines Manufacturing, you will lead senior managers and teams responsible for production, industrialization, and continuous improvement.

This hands-on leadership role balances the immediate need to deliver BE-4 engines with the work of bringing Northstar into production and scaling manufacturing capability for the future. You will partner across Blue Origin to deliver safely, reliably, on schedule, and at planned cost.

### **Responsibilities**

* Lead BE-4 and Northstar manufacturing in Huntsville, delivering to customer, program, safety, quality, schedule, and cost commitments.
* Sustain and improve BE-4 production while transitioning Northstar from development into stable, repeatable production.
* Develop production strategies, capacity plans, and operating rhythms aligned with program needs and company operating plans.
* Coordinate factory readiness, equipment identification and procurement, capital improvements, production start-up, and process qualification.
* Partner with Engineering, Program Management, Supply Chain, Test Operations, Quality, Safety, and other Blue Origin sites to resolve constraints and improve hardware flow.
* Lead improvement efforts across manufacturing, business processes, production planning, and resource utilization; apply lessons learned and standardize effective practices.
* Manage the manufacturing capital portfolio and ensure projects are executed safely and on schedule.
* Champion mission assurance and safety principles, including the planning and execution of critical operations.
* Develop leaders and teams, strengthen organizational capability, and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Identify opportunities to improve safety, quality, cost, capacity, and delivery performance. 

### **Minimum qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in industrial, manufacturing, mechanical, or electrical engineering, or equivalent experience.
* 15+ years of experience in aerospace or a closely related complex manufacturing industry.
* Significant experience leading manufacturing or production organizations, including through senior leaders.
* Experience managing customer relationships and expectations.
* Experience with program- or project-level financial performance, budgets, or profit and loss.
* Proven ability to lead complex projects, coordinate across functions, and deliver in a fast-paced environment.
* Expertise in production operations, manufacturing process development, and continuous improvement.
* Strong understanding of quality systems, root cause analysis, and risk-based problem solving.
* Demonstrated commitment to safety, including experience planning and overseeing critical operations.
Strong communication, judgment, personnel management, and mentoring skills. 

### **Preferred qualifications**

* Master’s degree in engineering or a related field; MBA or equivalent business experience.
* Experience transitioning complex products from development into production and scaling manufacturing rates.
* Experience launching or expanding a production facility.
* Knowledge of fabrication, assembly, integration, test, quality, and configuration management.
* Experience managing facility-level capital improvements and equipment procurement.
* Lean Manufacturing, Toyota Production System, or Six Sigma experience; Black Belt certification is a plus.
Experience leading operations across multiple departments, programs, or sites. 

 

**Culture Statement**

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 

**Export Control Regulations**

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 

**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical 

 

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
* Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws.

 

**Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation**

Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

identity_held_roles.title: Sr. Director, Additive Manufacturing Systems Engineering
identity_held_roles.description:
**Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future**
======================================

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

**Why This Role Exists**
------------------------

Hadrian is building an additive manufacturing capability that runs as part of an autonomous factory, not as a room full of printers. The hard problem is not any single machine, material, or line of code. It is making all of them behave as one system. Systems engineering is the glue that holds that system together, and this role owns the glue.

The Senior Director leads three engineering functions, materials and process engineering, hardware engineering, and software engineering, and is accountable for the digital backbone that binds them to each other and to applications engineering: the architecture, interfaces, and data that connect Hadrian’s Opus platform to cutting-edge additive manufacturing equipment, add automation where it makes sense, fuse sensor data into the part record, and turn a collection of parts into a full, integrated digital manufacturing system built around additive.

The measure of success is not three strong teams. It is one manufacturing system that a customer part flows through, from design intent to qualified hardware, with every decision and every data point captured along the way.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* **Architect the system.** Define and control the end-to-end architecture for additive at Hadrian: requirements, interfaces, data model, and acceptance criteria that hold across multiple equipment platforms, modalities, and sites. Treat the factory as the product.
* **Build the digital backbone.** Connect additive equipment, peripherals, and inspection assets to Opus with the same discipline a semiconductor fab applies to connecting tools to the host: standardized state models, telemetry, event streams, and data contracts, with security and configuration control built in.
* **Fuse the sensors.** Bring in-situ monitoring, machine telemetry, environmental data, and downstream inspection into one correlated record per part, then move from monitoring to data-driven release and, where it is justified, closed-loop control.
* **Automate where it pays.** Lead automation across additive cells (material and powder handling, build changeover, part removal and depowdering, post-processing flow, robotics, controls, and safety) with a written case for each: safety, repeatability, and data capture first; labor second. Never automate an unstable process.
* **Lead the three functions as one.** Set standards, priorities, and cadence for materials and process, hardware, and software engineering. Resolve conflicts between them at the architecture level, not the escalation level.
* **Own the applications engineering interface.** With the Head of Applications Engineering, define what a production-ready hand-off looks like, publish the process capability and design-rule data applications engineers build to, and close the loop from floor results back into design guidance.
* **Industrialize the equipment.** Through the hardware engineering leader, own factory and site acceptance, commissioning, reliability (preventive maintenance, spares, MTBF/MTTR), and configuration-controlled modification and upgrade of additive systems, and lead the technical relationships with equipment partners that unlock deeper integration. The machine-level depth lives in that team; the standards and the outcomes live here.
* **Design for the factory.** Partner with Factory Development and Factory Automation on cell and site design: material flow, capacity, simulation, utilities, and the path to lights-out operation for additive.
* **Build quality in.** Make the system itself the evidence: traceability, data integrity, and process control that stand up to AS9100 audits and customer qualification without a separate paper trail.
* **Be the additive voice in Hadrian’s platform.** Carry additive requirements into Core Engineering and the Opus roadmap, and bring platform capability back to the floor.
* **Hire, develop, and retain.** Build a leadership bench under you, set a high technical bar, and make Hadrian the place the best additive systems engineers in the country want to work.

**What We’re Looking For**
--------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a physical science; an advanced degree is strongly preferred.
* 12+ years in advanced manufacturing, with real depth in at least three of these six domains: factory design and industrial automation; semiconductor or other high-reliability capital-equipment engineering; manufacturing software and data systems; materials science and process engineering; quality systems in regulated industries; sensing, process monitoring, and sensor fusion.
* 5+ years leading engineering teams, including leading through managers and building at least one function from the ground up.
* Production experience with metal laser powder bed fusion, as a user of the equipment, a developer of it, or both.
* Has led the integration of complex equipment into factory-level software (manufacturing execution, equipment host, or data platforms), including requirements, interface standards, and acceptance criteria.
* Has taken at least one production automation or capital-equipment program (robotic cells, material handling, or equipment with safety systems and controls) from concept through commissioning in a regulated environment (aerospace and defense, semiconductor, medical, or similar), and has owned the reliability of production equipment afterward.
* Fluent across the stack: can review a process flow, a data schema, a metallurgical cross-section, and a controls narrative in the same meeting, and knows which one is lying.
* Has worked as a true peer to a customer-facing or design function, with a record of building clean interfaces rather than absorbing the other team.
* Willing to travel up to 20%, including to Hadrian sites and international partners. Must meet the ITAR requirements below.

**What Will Set You Apart**
---------------------------

* Ph.D. in materials science, mechanical engineering, systems engineering or a related discipline.
* Semiconductor capital-equipment background: equipment-to-host integration, tool matching, fleet data, fault detection and statistical process control at scale.
* Equipment-maker experience developing or launching metal additive systems (new product introduction, cost-productivity trades, design reviews) in addition to user-side experience.
* In-situ monitoring and sensor fusion implemented in production, with data-driven release or closed-loop control.
* Factory design: material flow planning, discrete-event simulation, and highly automated or lights-out operations.
* AS9100 and customer qualification pathways; familiarity with AM specifications (ASTM F42, ISO/ASTM 529xx, SAE AMS 7xxx series).
* Budget or P&L ownership of a capital-intensive program, with a record of making the build-versus-buy and automate-versus-wait calls well.
* Modern software fluency: APIs, event streaming, OT/IT architecture, industrial interoperability standards (OPC UA, MTConnect), and cloud data platforms.

**Compensation**
----------------

For this role, the target salary range is $300,000 - $350,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

**Benefits for Full-time Employees**
------------------------------------

* Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees
 
 401k
* Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need.
* Flexible vacation policy
* Equity

**ITAR Requirements**
---------------------

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

**Use of AI in hiring**
-----------------------

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy.

**Consideration of Criminal History**
-------------------------------------

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

**Hadrian Is An Equal Opportunity Employer**
--------------------------------------------

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

existing_roles.title: Vice President Quality Control
existing_roles.description:
Shape the future of quality and patient trust. Join us as the Vice President, Global Quality Control and lead a world-class laboratory network that powers our clinical and commercial programs across the globe. Reporting to the Chief Quality Officer, you will set the enterprise strategy and build a unified, high-performing Quality Control organization that delivers reliable data, inspection-ready laboratories, and timely product release support—while advancing standardization, digital innovation, scientific excellence, and operational performance.
  
  
**Company Overview**
The work we do at FUJIFILM Biotechnologies has never been more important—and we are looking for talented candidates to join us. We are growing our locations, our capabilities, and our teams, and looking for passionate, mission-driven people like you who want to make a real difference in people’s lives.
  
  
Join FUJIFILM Biotechnologies and help make the next vaccine, cure, or gene therapy in partnership with some of the most innovative biopharma companies across the globe. We are proud to cultivate a culture that will fuel your passion, energy, and drive - what we call Genki.
  
  
Fujifilm is globally headquartered in Tokyo with over 70,000 employees across four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging. We are guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles.” Visit: https://www.fujifilm.com/us/en/about/region/careers
  
  
**Job Description**
Your impact In this enterprise role, your leadership will directly influence patient safety, product quality, inspection outcomes, batch disposition timelines, and continuity of supply across a diverse global portfolio. You will advise senior executives on investment, capacity, technology, organizational design, and regulatory strategy—shaping multi‑year business and quality plans. Your decisions will strengthen client trust, accelerate revenue recognition, reduce the cost of quality, and protect the company’s license to operate.
  
  
What you will do
  
  

* Define and execute a global Quality Control strategy, operating model, and multi‑year roadmap across sites, modalities, and development phases. Establish enterprise standards, clear decision rights, and governance forums that enable consistent, phase‑appropriate control while allowing justified site or platform differences.
* Provide executive oversight of end‑to‑end Quality Control operations, including analytical, biochemical, biological, microbiological, raw‑material, in‑process, release, and stability testing; as well as environmental and utility monitoring. Ensure capacity, prioritization, and flawless execution to meet program milestones, product disposition, client commitments, and uninterrupted supply.
* Govern the analytical method lifecycle from early development through transfer, qualification, validation, comparability, continued performance verification, and retirement. Ensure control strategies and specifications evolve appropriately through clinical development, process performance qualification, launch, and sustained commercial supply.
* Set global expectations for current good manufacturing practice, applicable good laboratory practice principles, data governance, principles that ensure data are attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate and complete, laboratory investigations, out of specification and out of trend management, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, change control, and audit readiness. Lead enterprise strategy and executive response for regulatory inspections and critical client audits.
* Build and deliver the digital and technology roadmap for laboratory information management systems, electronic laboratory notebooks, laboratory execution systems, chromatography data systems, laboratory automation, advanced analytics, and instrument connectivity. Sponsor validated deployment, master‑data governance, cybersecurity, and adoption that improve right‑first‑time outcomes and cycle time.
* Direct enterprise Quality Control capacity planning, capital prioritization, make‑versus‑buy decisions, laboratory footprint strategy, and governance of external testing partners. Align resources and contingency plans with demand forecasts, technology transfers, new product introductions, and network resiliency needs.
* Establish enterprise metrics and management review for on‑time testing and release support, lead time, invalid results, out of specification and out of trend rates, investigation cycle time, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, stability execution, method performance, cost, and productivity. Drive risk‑based priorities, Lean practices, and cross‑site learning to deliver sustainable improvement.
* Serve as the senior Quality Control liaison for strategic clients, regulatory authorities, and executive governance. Translate complex laboratory, method, and compliance risks into clear business implications, negotiate technically sound solutions, and ensure commitments are realistic, documented, and delivered.
* Build and lead a global organization through senior leaders. Define capabilities and succession plans, develop technical career paths and communities of practice, and cultivate a culture of scientific rigor, transparency, accountability, inclusion, and proactive risk management.
* Own escalation and coordinated response for significant Quality Control events, laboratory constraints, critical data‑integrity concerns, assay failures, method or specification issues, and testing disruptions. Make or recommend risk‑based decisions on testing strategy, product impact, remediation, and continuity of supply.
* Perform other duties in support of the broader Global Quality strategy and company objectives.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline, with fifteen or more years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or contract development and manufacturing organization Quality Control; or a Master’s degree with ten or more years.
* Ten or more years of people leadership, including five or more years leading senior leaders with accountability for multiple laboratories, sites, or functional areas.
* Demonstrated leadership of Quality Control across development and commercial stages, including method transfer, qualification and validation, release and stability testing, microbiology, and environmental and utility monitoring.
* Proven experience with global regulatory inspections and client audits, and with complex out of specification, out of trend, data‑integrity, and laboratory‑compliance matters.
* Experience managing budgets, capital portfolios, headcount, capacity, external laboratories, and enterprise transformation in a matrixed global organization.
* Executive‑level communication and client‑facing experience in a regulated, technically complex environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced scientific degree and/or a Master of Business Administration.
* Global leadership within a contract development and manufacturing organization supporting biologics, vaccines, advanced therapies, or sterile manufacturing.
* Experience scaling Quality Control from clinical development through process performance qualification, launch, and sustained commercial supply.
* Working knowledge of the following: Food and Drug Administration; European Medicines Agency; Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency; Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency; International Council for Harmonisation guidelines Q2, Q5, Q6, Q9, Q10, and Q14; United States Pharmacopeia; European Pharmacopoeia; Japanese Pharmacopoeia; Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations Parts 210, 211, and 11; and European Union Good Manufacturing Practice Annexes 1 and 11; as well as applicable data‑integrity expectations.
* Experience deploying global laboratory information management systems and laboratory digitalization and automation.
* Credentials from the American Society for Quality, and training in Lean and Six Sigma or equivalent quality and operational excellence disciplines.

If you are a strategic, hands‑on executive who thrives at the intersection of science, operations, and leadership, we would love to hear from you. Apply today and help us raise the bar for quality worldwide.
  
  
The US salary range for this position is $272,000 to $325,000.  Pay within this range varies by work location and may also depend on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.
  
  
Our programs are designed to focus on maintaining and enhancing all pillars of health with a robust benefits package including medical, dental, vision and prescription drug coverage with the option of a Health Savings Account with company contributions. In addition, we offer an industry leading 401(k)savings plan, insurance coverage , employee assistance programs and various wellness incentives. We support life-work balance with paid vacation time, sick time, and company holidays. Explore a supportive environment that enriches both your personal and professional growth!
  
  
This is a global position that will support all our FUJIFILM Biotechnologies sites. Benefits and compensation will be governed by the location that you are based from and considered your home site.
  
  
As part of any recruitment process, FUJIFILM Biotechnologies collects and processes personal data relating to job applicants. The  or ganisation  is committed to being transparent about how it collects and uses that data  and to meeting its data protection obligations and may share this as part of the global recruitment process with hiring  managers in Europe and the United St ates.
  
  
To all agencies: Please, no phone calls or emails to any employee of FUJIFILM about this requisition. All resumes submitted by search firms/employment agencies to any employee at FUJIFILM via- email , the internet or in any form and/or method will be deemed the sole property of FUJIFILM, unless such search firms /employment agencies were engaged by FUJIFILM for this requisition and a valid agreement with FUJIFILM is in place. In the event a candidate who was submitted outside of the FUJIFILM agency engagement process is hired, no fee or payment of any kind will be paid.
  
  
**EEO Information**
Fujifilm is committed to providing equal opportunities in hiring, promotion and advancement, compensation, benefits, and training regardless of nationality, age, gender, sexual orientation or gender identity, race, ethnicity, religion, political creed, ideology, national, or social origin, disability, veteran status, etc.

If you require reasonable accommodation in completing this application, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participating in the employee selection process, please direct your inquiries to our HR Department (fdbglobaltalent@fujifilm.com).

existing_roles.description:
**Executive Director / VP of Quality**

I’m partnering exclusively with a growing Pharmaceutical Company looking to bring on a Vice President of Quality to lead its entire site Quality organisation, reporting directly to the CEO.

This is a senior, high-impact leadership opportunity for an established Quality executive to shape the site's Quality strategy, strengthen regulatory compliance and build a scalable Quality organisation as the business enters its next phase of growth and investment.

The successful individual will have oversight of both Quality Assurance and Quality Control, with significant influence across manufacturing operations, regulatory affairs, product development and wider business strategy. This is an opportunity to take genuine ownership of the Quality function, work closely with executive leadership and help drive the business forward while maintaining the highest standards of product quality and patient safety.

**Key areas of responsibility:**

* Set the overall Quality vision, objectives and priorities for the site, leading both QA and QC and ensuring the function supports business growth, operational performance and regulatory compliance.
* Act as the senior Quality representative to the FDA, leading inspections, maintaining inspection readiness, managing regulatory responses and overseeing sustainable remediation where required.
* Own the effectiveness and continuous improvement of the site QMS, ensuring systems remain robust, risk-based and aligned with evolving regulatory expectations.
* Provide executive oversight of batch release, deviations, investigations, CAPAs, change control, complaints, supplier quality, document control and data integrity, maintaining appropriate independent Quality decision-making.
* Oversee analytical and microbiological testing, OOS investigations, stability programmes, laboratory systems, environmental monitoring and associated compliance requirements.
* Partner with Manufacturing, Operations, Regulatory Affairs, R&D and Engineering to provide Quality oversight across product development, technology transfer, validation, commercial manufacturing and post-market activities.
* Establish meaningful Quality metrics, lead management reviews and use trend analysis, root-cause investigations and risk-based decision-making to address systemic issues and improve site performance.
* Build, lead and develop a high-performing Quality organisation, establishing the appropriate structure, technical capabilities, succession planning and resources to support the site's future needs.
* Work directly with the CEO and wider leadership team, translating complex regulatory requirements and Quality risks into practical business decisions while protecting compliance and patient safety.

**Qualifications & Experience**

* 12+ years of progressive experience within pharmaceutical manufacturing, with substantial Quality leadership experience in sterile pharmaceutical products.
* Proven executive-level leadership across multidisciplinary Quality organisations, ideally with responsibility for both QA and QC.
* A strong track record of leading FDA inspections, managing regulatory interactions and driving successful inspection readiness and remediation programmes.
* In-depth knowledge of US pharmaceutical cGMP requirements, particularly 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211, with familiarity with relevant medical device regulations.
* Broad expertise across QMS, CAPA, validation and qualification, laboratory operations, supplier quality, complaints, risk management and data integrity.
* Experience supporting products throughout the lifecycle, from development and regulatory submissions through commercial manufacturing, release and post-market activities.
* Demonstrated success building Quality teams, developing future leaders and embedding a culture of accountability, compliance and continuous improvement.
* The ability to operate as a strategic business partner to executive leadership while maintaining the independence and authority required of the Quality function.
* A degree in a relevant scientific or technical discipline is required.

Apply today to learn more or reach out directly with your CV to rbanton@barringtonjames.com

existing_roles.title: Vice President, Global GMP Quality
existing_roles.description:
**MISSION**

Mirum Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming the treatment of rare diseases. We are passionate about advancing scientific discoveries to become important medicines for rare disease patients. We are collaborative, creative, and experienced professionals and we’re looking to augment our team with other individuals who embody our values: care, be real, get it done, and have fun, seriously.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The VP, Global GMP Quality position will be responsible for leading the GMP quality functional teams at Mirum and its subsidiaries (US and International). This position will play a pivotal role in steering the organization toward an ongoing commitment to quality improvement, driving efforts to identify areas for optimization, innovation, and excellence. This person will be responsible for managing, mentoring and supporting a GMP Operations team of clinical and commercial Quality Assurance (QA) and Quality Control (QC) professionals. This person will provide leadership and hands-on support to ensure the seamless execution of GMP QA and QC functions, including product quality complaint investigation, root-cause investigations, and the reporting of critical GMP issues to executive management.  This person will also be responsible for leading, providing direction, resources, and guidance to ensure that all GMP quality processes are executed with the highest standards of compliance with FDA, EMA, and other international regulatory requirements, corporate objectives, and industry best practices. This role also involves ensuring that the GMP and GDP quality functions are closely aligned with the organization’s broader strategic goals, guaranteeing that quality initiatives support the company’s mission, vision, and operational objectives.

**JOB FUNCTIONS/RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Serve as the GMP quality strategic leader to assist the head of quality to further develop the quality culture at Mirum to be compliant, collaborative and phase appropriate.
* Develop and execute a global GMP quality strategy to align with corporate goals and regulatory requirements.
* Serve as the GMP quality strategic leader within the Quality group to lead the GMP QA and QC functional teams in fostering professional development and guiding staff in all aspects of GMP/GDP competence in meeting domestic and international regulatory requirements and guidelines (FDA, EMA, MHRA, NMPA, ICH, etc.).
* Lead the development and optimization of key processes, functional collaboration, transformational initiatives, and operational excellence through the GMP/GDP Quality Unit.
* Serve as the GMP quality lead in Audits and Regulatory Inspections in providing strategic leadership, interactions, responses, CAPA plans and implementation.
* Lead the GMP inspection readiness for the Company including GMP Quality improvement and maintenance.

**Job Summary**
The
**Director, Manufacturing Process Development**
will develop, characterize, scale, validate, transfer, and optimize manufacturing processes for dental consumables globally. This role translates product, chemistry, material, quality, and customer requirements into robust, compliant, cost-effective manufacturing processes within an FDA- and ISO-regulated environment.
  
  
Reporting to the VP, Innovation & R&D, this leader bridges R&D Engineering, Manufacturing, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, and Procurement, driving manufacturing readiness, technical risk management, and process ownership. The role leads a team of engineers and requires strong influence, relationship-building, and cross-functional navigation skills.
  
  
*Candidate must reside within a commutable distance to Pomona, CA. This is not a hybrid or remote opportunity and requires onsite presence 4 days per week.*
**Primary Duties & Responsibilities**

* Develop process development strategy and roadmaps aligned to business and portfolio priorities, setting standards, governance, and resourcing for development, scale-up, validation, and lifecycle support.
* Lead, coach, and develop a process engineering team, building technical depth, accountability, and succession planning.
* Develop scalable manufacturing platforms, standards, and reusable process technologies to accelerate future product introductions and operational excellence.
* Drive development and adoption of innovative manufacturing technologies and automation solutions to improve scalability, quality, efficiency, and competitive advantage.
* Partner with product development teams to embed design-for-manufacturability principles early in product and formulation development.
* Own process development from feasibility through validation and transfer for adhesives, composites, cements, endodontic, and other dental consumable platforms, defining process specifications, critical parameters, and controls.
* In collaboration with Chemistry team, characterize material and process behavior (e.g., rheology, mixing, variability, hold times) to build scientific understanding linking materials, equipment, and finished-product performance.
* Apply Design of Experiments (DOE), statistical analysis, and risk-based tools to define process design spaces, control strategies, and acceptance criteria.
* Identify, assess, and mitigate manufacturing, scale-up, and commercialization risks throughout the product lifecycle.
* Lead pilot builds, scale-up, qualification, validation, and manufacturing transfer, ensuring readiness criteria, documentation, and training are in place.
* Provide process development leadership on New Product Development (NPD), commercialization, and lifecycle teams, aligning scope, risk, resources, and timelines across functions.
* Serve as the key technical liaison between Manufacturing and R&D, building trust and alignment across functions without relying on positional authority.
* Partner with Operations and Engineering to optimize processes, troubleshoot issues, and improve capability across the product lifecycle, clarifying handoffs from development to routine manufacturing.
* Collaborate on investigations into nonconformances, deviations, and quality events using root-cause analysis and statistical methods to drive effective CAPAs.
* Define equipment and process requirements and partner with cross-functional teams and vendors on selection, integration, and automation to improve safety, quality, and efficiency.
* Drive measurable improvements in yield, throughput, cycle time, capability, and cost through continuous improvement initiatives.
* Ensure all activities comply with the Quality Management System (QMS), FDA requirements, ISO 13485, GMP, EH&S, and applicable SOPs; support audits, CAPAs, and regulatory submissions.
* Communicate strategy, readiness, risk, and outcomes to senior leadership, ensuring sound documentation and escalation practices.
* Travel approximately 25% domestically and internationally to support manufacturing sites.

**Incidental Duties:**
The above statements describe the general nature and level of work being performed in this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, and additional responsibilities may be assigned, as required, by management.
  
  
**Job Requirements**
**Qualifications:**
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. This individual must be able to function in a fast-paced environment where priorities may change rapidly. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
  
  
**Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Polymer Science, Chemistry, Biomedical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related discipline required; master’s degree or PhD preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience across developing, scaling, or validating manufacturing processes in a regulated or formal quality-system environment is required.
* 5+ years of people and cross-functional leadership experience required.
* Experience in supporting multi-site or global manufacturing operations preferred.
* Experience with Lean manufacturing or Six Sigma tools and/or methodologies required.

**Skills/Abilities**

* Demonstrated ability to influence without authority, gain commitment, and lead through relationships, technical credibility, data, and shared business objectives required.
* Exceptional relationship-building and collaboration skills, with a demonstrated ability to create alignment and trust between Manufacturing and R&D required.
* Strong people leadership skills with a record of developing technical talent, building capability, setting clear expectations, and driving accountability required.
* Advanced problem-solving and analytical skills, including Design of Experiments (DOE), statistical analysis, process capability, root-cause analysis, and risk-based decision making required.
* Demonstrated ability to lead complex programs, prioritize resources, manage ambiguity, resolve conflict, and drive execution across functions and sites required.
* Strong business and operational acumen, including the ability to balance safety, quality, compliance, delivery, innovation, capacity, and cost required.
* Strong verbal, presentation, facilitation, and technical writing skills in English, with the ability to communicate effectively from the manufacturing floor through executive leadership required.

existing_roles.description:
**Job Summary**
The Director, Advanced Shipbuilding & Manufacturing Excellence is Gulf Copper's industrial design authority and the leader of its continuous improvement program. The Director owns the production-system concept for each Gulf Copper site in Galveston, Port Arthur, and Corpus Christi, Texas: how work flows through the yard, how material moves, what equipment and tooling are used, and how the facility is laid out to support it. On the front end, the Director defines the production-system, equipment, and layout requirements that the architect/engineering firm and construction manager design to, and leads the selection of production equipment and tooling. On an ongoing basis, the Director leads the company's effort to continuously improve shipbuilding, ship repair, and module fabrication methods, tooling, work content, and productivity across all sites, and investigates and introduces proven advanced manufacturing technologies including automation, robotics, digital shipbuilding, and artificial intelligence (AI). The role supports Gulf Copper's growth into construction of U.S. Navy (USN) and U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) vessels, government and commercial ship repair, and distributed fabrication of ship and submarine modules.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

This position is responsible for the following: Other duties may be assigned.

**Production-System Design Authority (Front End)**

* Own the production-system concept for each site, including process flow, material flow, shop and work-station arrangement, build strategy, and facility layout, and hold design authority over these elements within the facility modernization master plan.
* Define and approve the production-system, throughput, equipment, and layout requirements that the architect/engineering firm and construction manager design to, and review their deliverables for conformance to those requirements.
* Lead the specification, evaluation, and selection of production equipment and tooling, including heavy lift and cranes, panel and block assembly lines, cutting and welding systems, blast and paint facilities, material handling, and ship transfer and launch systems, including trade studies, vendor evaluation, and total-cost-of-ownership analysis.
* Define the role and target capacity of each facility (newbuild, repair, module fabrication, outfitting, and support) and the production-system requirements needed to achieve them, as input to capital sequencing decisions.
* Translate target vessel classes and customer requirements into facility and process requirements, including ship size, displacement, launch and transfer method, assembly sequence, test and trials, and delivery.
* Work with finance, business development, and the Grants and Workforce Development managers to develop business cases and cost models for production-system and equipment investments.

**Continuous Improvement & Industrial Engineering**

* Lead Gulf Copper's continuous improvement program across all sites, establishing the methodology, governance, cadence, and reporting for improvement of shipbuilding, ship repair, and module fabrication processes.
* Establish and maintain productivity baselines and targets (such as man-hours per ton, cycle time, first-pass yield, rework, and schedule adherence) by site, product line, and process, and report progress against them.
* Lead value-stream mapping, work measurement, line balancing, and takt-based planning for fabrication, assembly, outfitting, and repair processes.
* Develop, document, and sustain standard work, production standards, procedures, and work instructions that reflect current best methods, tooling, and facilities.
* Lead cross-functional improvement events and projects with yard operations, engineering, planning, quality, and supply chain, and track resulting savings against investment.
* Operate a lessons-learned loop that feeds production experience back into layout, equipment, tooling, and build-strategy decisions.
* Set methods, standards, and tooling for the yards; General Managers retain ownership of daily production execution.

**Advanced Technology: Automation, Robotics, Digital Shipbuilding & AI**

* Investigate, evaluate, and benchmark new shipbuilding technologies and methods through industry research, domestic and international shipyard visits, vendor engagement, and partnerships with government and academic organizations.
* Develop business cases, pilot programs, and implementation plans for new technologies, and lead implementation of proven techniques such as robotic and automated welding, cutting, and panel and module production lines.
* Evaluate and pilot AI, data analytics, and digital shipbuilding tools for production planning, scheduling, quality, and productivity improvement, and scale those that demonstrate value.
* Work with engineering, IT, and operations to integrate new technologies with design, production control, and quality systems.
* Partner with the Workforce Development Manager to train and upskill the workforce to operate and maintain new methods and technologies.

**Module Fabrication & Distributed Manufacturing**

* Define the production-system and facility requirements for complex module fabrication, including large steel, piping, outfitting, and system modules for surface ships and submarines.
* Establish standard processes for module design interfaces, tolerances, dimensional control, quality assurance, transportation, and integration across Gulf Copper sites and outside partners.
* Define the production approach and facility requirements for a distributed manufacturing model in which modules are built across Gulf Copper's Texas facilities and with partners, then transported and integrated at the final assembly site.

**Leadership, Collaboration & Reporting**

* Lead the industrial engineering and continuous improvement staff and matrixed engineering, planning, and project personnel assigned to advanced shipbuilding initiatives.
* Coordinate with yard General Managers, engineering, estimating, supply chain, quality, and safety to implement new methods, tooling, and equipment and to prepare the yards for new shipbuilding and repair work.
* Provide facility, capacity, production-approach, and productivity input to business development, capture, and proposal teams for USN, USCG, and commercial opportunities, and serve as technical subject-matter expert on production capability in customer and partner discussions.
* Prepare reports and presentations for executive leadership on production-system design status, equipment selection, continuous improvement results, technology initiatives, and facility readiness.
* Establish metrics and systems for tracking production-system milestones, equipment procurement, productivity, and capacity.

**Safety & Quality**

* Ensure new facilities, equipment, tooling, and methods are designed for safety and comply with applicable environmental, safety, and permitting requirements.
* Design processes and quality systems to meet NAVSEA, USCG, and classification society standards applicable to shipbuilding and ship repair, working with the Quality organization.
* Promote a strong safety culture in the introduction of new methods and technologies.

**Key Measures of Success:**

* Production-system concept, layout requirements, and equipment list approved for each site by the dates set in the facility modernization master plan.
* Productivity baselines established for each site and product line within the first year, with annual improvement targets set and met thereafter.
* Documented continuous improvement savings tracked against capital and program investment.
* Pilot-to-adoption rate and realized benefit of new technologies introduced.
* Standard work and production standards in place and maintained for modernized processes.

**Required Education & Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Industrial/Manufacturing Engineering, Naval Architecture, Marine Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Engineering Management, or related field. Master's degree preferred.
* Minimum of 12 years of progressive experience in shipbuilding or heavy industrial manufacturing, including at least 7 years in shipbuilding, ship repair, or marine module fabrication.
* Demonstrated experience leading continuous improvement, lean manufacturing, or industrial engineering programs in a production environment with measurable productivity results.
* Demonstrated experience defining production-system, equipment, or facility layout requirements for shipyard or heavy industrial facility modernization or expansion.
* Strong knowledge of modern shipbuilding production methods, including modular and zone construction, panel and block assembly, outfitting, and ship assembly and launch.
* Experience evaluating and implementing automation, robotics, or other advanced manufacturing technologies in a production environment.
* Knowledge of NAVSEA, USCG, and classification society standards applicable to shipbuilding and ship repair.
* Strong project management, budgeting, and scheduling skills.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; experience with project scheduling and shipbuilding design and production software preferred.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent continuous improvement certification.
* Experience with first-of-class production-system design for a greenfield or major brownfield shipyard stand-up, including panel line or block assembly line design.
* Experience constructing large, complex USN or USCG vessels such as icebreakers, combatants, or auxiliaries.
* Experience with distributed manufacturing of ship or submarine modules, including submarine industrial base programs.
* Experience benchmarking production methods at domestic and international shipyards.
* Experience with AI, digital shipbuilding, digital twin, or data-driven production planning tools.
* Experience with construction management or general contractor delivery models for large industrial facility projects.
* Prior senior leadership experience in shipyard operations, engineering, or production.

**Working Conditions:**

* Remote position.
* Regular travel among Gulf Copper's Galveston, Port Arthur, and Corpus Christi facilities, and to customer, supplier, partner, and industry sites, including international shipyard benchmarking.
* May require extended hours to meet project, customer, and production milestones.

**Necessary Equipment Operation:**

* Computer skills: MS Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) and project scheduling software.
* Ability to review and use engineering, CAD, and 3D model information.
* Office equipment, including telephone, scanner, computer printer, etc.
* Personal protective equipment (PPE) required when working in shipyard areas.

**Special Skills:**

* Ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams and drive sustained process improvement across multiple sites.
* Ability to evaluate and champion new methods and technologies and drive organizational change.
* Ability to think strategically over a 3–10 year horizon while delivering near-term improvement results.
* Ability to have difficult conversations with internal and external stakeholders.
* Ability to motivate employees and build a high-performing team.
* Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
* Ability to work under deadlines and schedule pressures.
* Commitment to company values, policies, procedures, and safety programs.

\* An Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability. Know Your Rights. If you’d like to view a copy of the company’s affirmative action plan or policy statement, please email: hrcorp@gulfcopper.com.  If you have a disability and you believe you need a reasonable accommodation in order to search for a job opening or to submit an online application, please e-mail: hrcorp@gulfcopper.com.

Are you interested in being part of an innovative team that supports Westinghouse's mission to provide clean energy solutions? At Westinghouse, we recognize that our employees are our most valuable asset and we seek to identify, attract and recruit the most qualified talent while recognizing and encouraging the value of diversity in the global workplace.
  
  
**About The Role**
As a Senior Manager, LEU+ Manufacturing Process Engineering you will lead process engineering for the LEU+ Manufacturing Program, a capital expansion of Westinghouse's Columbia Fuel Fabrication Facility to manufacture LEU+ (higher-enrichment low-enriched uranium) nuclear fuel. Accountable for the design, qualification and startup of the new manufacturing processes, including uranium conversion, pellet production, fuel rod and assembly manufacturing, uranium recovery and recycling, and the laboratory and maintenance areas. Plans and directs the methods, equipment and processes needed to deliver safe, high-quality, cost-effective fuel, and develops the engineers who deliver them.
  
  
You will report to the Project Director, LEU+ Manufacturing Program and be located at Columbia, SC. You will support this role 100% onsite.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the LEU+ Process Engineering organization with responsibility for safety, regulatory compliance, product quality, technical execution, cost, schedule, and operational readiness.
* Lead process engineering activities supporting nuclear safety, including Integrated Safety Analysis, hazard analysis, IROFS, criticality safety, NRC licensing activities, and regulatory change control.
* Oversee process engineering deliverables from initial design through equipment procurement, installation, commissioning, qualification, startup, and turnover to Operations.
* Ensure manufacturing equipment and processes meet product quality, nuclear safety, performance, and qualification requirements.
* Lead mechanical, chemical, and process engineering resources while forecasting staffing needs and assigning technical ownership.
* Coordinate technical interfaces across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Procurement, Construction, Commissioning, Automation/IT, and suppliers.
* Manage process engineering scope, budget, schedule, risks, and change control while providing clear status reporting to program leadership.
* Guide manufacturing optimization using Lean/Six Sigma, OEE, capacity analysis, bottleneck reduction, and continuous improvement.
* Support operational readiness through procedures, training, spare-parts planning, startup support, and turnover of qualified manufacturing processes.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Chemical, Mechanical, Nuclear Engineering, or related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in process engineering, manufacturing, plant operations, capital projects, or related technical leadership.
* 5+ years of people-management experience leading engineers and managing technical resources and budgets.
* Demonstrated leadership of complex, diverse engineering or manufacturing programs with accountability for safety, quality, cost, schedule, and technical performance.
* Knowledge of process engineering, process safety, hazard analysis, manufacturing systems, and equipment/process qualification.

* Knowledge of nuclear fuel manufacturing processes, including conversion, pelleting, rod/assembly manufacturing, or uranium recovery, preferred.

* Lean Six Sigma experience required; Black Belt certification preferred.

We are committed to transparency and equity in all of our people practices. The base salary range for this position, which is dependent upon experience, qualifications and skills, is estimated to be $144,000 to $180,000 per year.

Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI ) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. Reporting to the Wafer Fab General Manager, the
**Senior Manager, Production – Fab Operations**
will lead our ~300‑employee Production organization—including Production Managers, Supervisors, Trainers, 5S & Continuous Improvement, New Product Technicians, Leads, and Operators—who execute day‑to‑day manufacturing, testing, and shipping of a broad product portfolio as the fab continues to ramp, expand, and modernize a facility with over 25 years of operational history.
  
  
Apply now for the opportunity to grow your career and help innovate ahead of what’s possible.
  
  
**Job Duties**
The Senior Manager, Production – Fab Operations is a senior operations leader responsible for translating site strategy into strong operational execution. Responsibilities are aligned to three core competency areas:
  
  
**Operational & Strategic Execution**

* Lead the execution of production improvement roadmaps, supporting longer‑term digital transformation, automation, and modernization initiatives defined at the site level.

* Provide clear tactical direction through written reports, dashboards, presentations, daily operational reviews, all‑hands meetings, and shift‑level stand‑ups, ensuring decisions are grounded in accurate, timely data.

* Develop production supervisors and frontline leaders capable of operating in an increasingly digital, automated, and data‑driven manufacturing environment.
* Execute effective performance management processes to improve team continuity, leadership capability, and operational results.
* Partner with Human Resources to support competency development, technical capability building, and training plans aligned with future manufacturing needs.
* Ensure alignment with ADI Enterprise Excellence Guiding Principles, emphasizing safety, quality, operational rigor, and responsible innovation.

**SCHEDULE**
This is an exempt role, working on‑site in Camas, Washington, primarily Monday through Friday, supporting a 24x7 continuous operation.
  
  
Occasional night or weekend hours are required to support operational needs.
